doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

chapter: The Bay Area scene and tastes
title: Racial tensions among Bay Area musicians
summary: He thinks race is less of an issue in San Francisco than elsewhere, though cliques exist.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Is there, or has there been, any issue with racial tensions between musicians here or audiences or anything like that over the years?

Well I mean I think it exists everywhere to a subtle degree. But I think it’s easier here than it is in a lot of places as far as musicians working with each other — black musicians and white musicians working together. It’s not an issue, to tell the truth, it’s just not. There are so-called cliques everywhere, people that have people they like to play with, and that exists here just like it does everywhere, and sometimes it seems to be an exclusive black clique or an exclusive white clique. But I don’t think that that’s — it wasn’t set up that way it’s just the way it happens because people like to play — but I mean I worked with a lot of different races. I mean black people, I worked with John Handy, I worked with Vernon Alley, I mean it’s not as — what’s the word — as overt as it is — I’ve talked to people in New York apparently it’s a little more lined, you know, divisive.
